observation_summary: The compiler incorrectly reordered associative operators (like *, /, %) during code generation, leading to incorrect operator precedence and associativity in the output JS.
reasoning_summary: The bug involves incorrect handling of operator associativity during code generation and peephole optimization. The fix involved removing an incorrect associativity check in CodeGenerator and implementing a new rotation algorithm (tryRotateAssociativeOperator) in PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax to correctly handle associative operator trees. This is a procedural/algorithmic correction to how the compiler transforms the AST.
evidence_used: The fix removes an incorrect associativity check in CodeGenerator.
The fix adds a new method tryRotateAssociativeOperator to PeepholeSubstituteAlternateSyntax to correctly reorder associative operator nodes.
The bug report states that *, / and % were not being handled correctly regarding left-to-right associativity.
The failing tests show incorrect output for associative operator combinations.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the fix involves the relationship between nodes in the AST, the root cause is the incorrect implementation of the associativity logic (the algorithm) used to transform those nodes.
The fix is a local procedural correction to existing compiler passes, not a design-level capability omission.
